Search the public API

The authored search and generated index search stay synchronized. Common entry terms include device, command list, resource, and descriptor.

How to read this reference

Namespaces

Lifecycle, shaders, pipelines, logging, and presentation live in arda::backend. Backend-neutral GPU types and interfaces live in arda::rhi. Qualified names show the owning namespace or type; short names are convenient search terms but may match overloads or members in several types.

Status and result conventions

A bool result reports whether an operation was accepted or completed according to its contract; read the Returns and Errors rows for the precise meaning. Result and status enums carry richer outcomes where a binary answer is insufficient. A successful call can still require later GPU synchronization, so success does not imply that queued work has finished.

Ownership and threading notation

The Ownership row says whether an argument is borrowed, copied, retained, transferred, or returned through an intrusive reference. “Caller-owned” means the caller must preserve the object for the stated lifetime. The Threading row distinguishes externally serialized process-wide operations, thread-safe APIs, recording-thread restrictions, and GPU ordering requirements. These contracts are part of the API, not optional guidance.

Descriptor naming

Types named *Desc, *Descriptor, *CreateInfo, or *Initializer collect configuration rather than representing a live GPU object. Their member-variable entries document defaults, validity, and relationships. Resource and state objects created from them can have different ownership and synchronization rules.

Signatures and entries

Each entry begins with its qualified symbol name and declaration. Parameter rows describe individual inputs when source documentation provides them. Returns, Ownership, Errors, Threading, Source, and Audience appear only when recorded. Overloads have separate stable IDs even when their qualified names are identical.

Header choice

Include ArdaBackend.h for the aggregate public surface or a focused public header for narrower dependencies.

Backend module provider contract

class

arda::backend::IArdaBackendModule
class IArdaBackendModule

Contract implemented by every statically or dynamically linkable backend module.

A module publishes identity and capabilities, creates a backend runtime and RHI provider, and participates in shader compilation. Registration is explicit and module lifetime must outlive every registry and active-runtime use.

Returns
Not applicable.
Ownership
The process registry borrows the module; the library or host retains ownership.
Errors
Invalid inputs, unavailable compilation, stale or missing artifacts, and backend persistence failures are reported through the declared status, result, diagnostic, or fallback behavior.
Threading
Process-wide compiler and registration operations serialize shared state; device and global-map operations require the synchronization and quiescence documented by their containing types.
Source
Source/ArdaBackend/Public/ArdaBackendProvider.h
arda::backend::IArdaBackendRuntime
class IArdaBackendRuntime

Owns the module-private runtime state that accompanies an RHI device.

Ownership
Owning handles retain their object; pointer and reference parameters are borrowed unless stated otherwise.
Errors
Failures and unsupported operations use the declared FArdaRHIStatus or TArdaRHIResult contract.
Threading
Calls follow the synchronization rules of the owning provider device or command list.
Source
Source/ArdaBackend/Public/ArdaBackendProvider.h

constant

arda::backend::ArdaBackendProviderInterfaceVersion
inline constexpr uint32_t ArdaBackendProviderInterfaceVersion = 4

Identifies the C++ provider ABI contract expected by this ArdaBackend build.

A linked module publishes the same value in its descriptor. Registration rejects descriptors compiled for a different interface revision so incompatible virtual contracts never become selectable.

Returns
Not applicable.
Ownership

arda::backend::ConfigureBackend
[[nodiscard]] bool ConfigureBackend(const FArdaBackendConfiguration& configuration)

Replaces the backend configuration before initialization.

Replaces either the complete process-wide configuration or only the selected backend before initialization. The change is accepted only while lifecycle state permits reconfiguration; the remaining configuration is preserved by the backend-only overload.

Parameter
const FArdaBackendConfiguration& configuration
Returns
True when the configuration was accepted.
Ownership
The configuration is copied. IArdaDiagnosticCallback remains caller-owned and must outlive every backend use that can report through it.
Errors
Returns false when configuration cannot be changed in the current lifecycle state.
Threading
Process-wide backend configuration and lifetime operations must be externally serialized and must not run concurrently with device use.

arda::backend::InitializeBackend

Initializes the configured backend for headless use.

Returns
True when a headless backend was initialized successfully.
Ownership
On success the process-wide backend owns the device context; callers receive retained RHI references through GetDevice or GetDeviceContext.
Errors
Returns false on shader directory failure, unavailable backend, validation or native device failure; GetBackendError provides the latest diagnostic.
Threading
Process-wide backend configuration and lifetime operations must be externally serialized and must not run concurrently with device use.

arda::backend::FArdaComputeOperand::RegisterCuda
[[nodiscard]] rhi::FArdaRHIStatus RegisterCuda(eastl::string Name, uint32_t MinimumArchitecture, uint32_t MaximumArchitecture, FArdaComputeKernelBuilder Builder)

Registers a CUDA builder without invoking it or requiring a CUDA-enabled device.

Name
Nonempty variant name, unique across CUDA and graphics registrations.
MinimumArchitecture
Inclusive SM lower bound, encoded as major * 10 + minor.
MaximumArchitecture
Inclusive SM upper bound; UINT32_MAX removes the upper bound.
Builder
Nonempty callback that builds ordered kernels from a validated invocation.
Returns
Success after storage; InvalidArgument for an empty/duplicate name, empty callback, or MinimumArchitecture greater than MaximumArchitecture. Rejection adds nothing.
Ownership
The callback is moved into the operand. Value captures live until operand destruction; reference captures must outlive every dispatch. The invocation is borrowed only for the callback duration and must not be retained by reference.
Errors
Registration validates metadata only; PTX and native launch failures occur at dispatch.
Threading
Register during construction before publishing the operand. Registration must not race with registration, selection or dispatch; callbacks must support any concurrent dispatches the application permits, on separately serialized command lists.
Source
Source/ArdaBackend/Public/Compute/ArdaComputeOperand.h
arda::backend::FArdaComputeOperand::RegisterGraphics
[[nodiscard]] rhi::FArdaRHIStatus RegisterGraphics(eastl::string Name, FArdaComputeShaderDispatch Dispatch)

Registers a compute-shader alternative usable without CUDA.

Name
Nonempty variant name, unique across both implementation families.
Dispatch
Nonempty callback responsible for transitions, pipeline/binding setup and recording.
Returns
Success after storage; InvalidArgument for an empty/duplicate name or empty callback.
Ownership
The operand owns the moved callback and its value captures. Reference captures must outlive its dispatches; recorded GPU dependencies must survive queue completion.
Errors
Callback failure is propagated by Dispatch without trying another implementation.
Threading
Register before publishing; do not race registration with dispatch. Callback code must support the application's concurrency and serialize each command list.
Source

ARDA_CHECK
#define ARDA_CHECK(Condition) \ do \ { \ (void)sizeof(Condition); \ } while (false)

Compiles out a fatal condition check without evaluating it.

Compiles out a fatal condition check without evaluating it. Expansion behavior and arguments are represented by the source-faithful macro signature; arguments may be evaluated according to the expansion. Conditional alternative: #define ARDA_CHECK(Condition) \ do \ { \ if (!(Condition)) \ { \ ::arda::backend::ReportFatalCheck( \ #Condition, \ __FILE__, \ static_cast<std::uint32_t>(__LINE__), \ __func__); \ } \ } while (false). Verifies a condition when checks are enabled and terminates on failure. Expansion behavior and arguments are represented by the source-faithful macro signature; arguments may be evaluated according to the expansion.

Parameter
Condition
Errors
Fatal failures are logged and terminate the process.

arda::backend::IArdaExternalDeviceProvider
class IArdaExternalDeviceProvider

Supplies one externally owned native graphics device.

Supplies one externally owned native graphics device. The provider remains host-owned. Arda copies the selected device descriptor and shared lifetime token before initialization returns; provider callbacks run under the registry lock and must not reenter.

Ownership
The provider pointer is non-owning and the host must keep it alive until it is unregistered after shutdown.
Threading
Provider callbacks execute while the backend registry lock is held. Implementations must not reenter backend registration or lifetime APIs.
Source

arda::backend::IArdaExternalResourceProvider
class IArdaExternalResourceProvider

Resolves stable external resource identifiers into native import descriptors.

Resolves stable external resource identifiers into complete native import descriptors. The provider remains host-owned, callbacks run under the registry lock, and Vulkan providers must enforce raw-handle lifetime and external synchronization.

Ownership
The provider pointer is non-owning and must remain valid while registered.
Threading
Resolve callbacks execute under the resource-provider registry lock and must not reenter this registry. The host must prevent concurrent provider unregistration.

arda::backend::ImportExternalBuffer
[[nodiscard]] rhi::TArdaRHIResult<rhi::FArdaRHIBufferRef> ImportExternalBuffer(const char* ProviderName, uint64_t Id)

Resolves and imports an external buffer into the active RHI device.

Resolves and imports an external buffer into the active RHI device. The imported wrapper retains mLifetimeToken. Reusing the same native handle with a different token is a descriptor conflict. External presentation is not supported by the current external wrapper; the host should import frame images and manage present.

Parameter
const char* ProviderName
Parameter
uint64_t Id
Returns
Imported buffer and status using normal RHI result conventions.
Ownership
The returned intrusive reference owns the imported wrapper; the wrapper retains the descriptor shared lifetime token but does not otherwise assume host-native ownership.
Errors
Returns status for missing providers, backend mismatch, resolution failure, invalid descriptors, descriptor conflicts, or unsupported imports.
Threading
Resolve callbacks execute under the resource-provider registry lock and must not reenter this registry. The host must prevent concurrent provider unregistration. Vulkan raw handles additionally require host lifetime and external synchronization.
Source

arda::backend::FArdaPipelineStateCache::FArdaPipelineStateCache
explicit FArdaPipelineStateCache( rhi::FArdaRHIDeviceRef Device, FArdaPipelineStateCacheConfiguration Configuration = {})

Creates a cache permanently bound to one RHI device.

Creates a cache permanently bound to one RHI device. Construction follows the defaults and ownership-bearing argument types shown in the declaration.

Parameter
rhi::FArdaRHIDeviceRef Device
Parameter
FArdaPipelineStateCacheConfiguration Configuration = {}
Ownership
Takes and retains an intrusive owning device reference for the entire cache lifetime.
Errors
Construction does not report status; individual lookup and creation operations return FArdaRHIStatus and retain diagnostics on failure.
Threading
The pipeline state cache is thread-safe for concurrent requests; destruction waits for internal operations to finish. The bound RHI device must remain valid for the cache lifetime.

destructor

arda::backend::FArdaPipelineStateCache::~FArdaPipelineStateCache
~FArdaPipelineStateCache()

Releases the cache and waits for internal operations to finish.

Releases the cache and waits for internal operations to finish. Destruction ends the object lifetime and releases state owned by the implementation.

Ownership
Releases cached pipeline references and the retained device after internal operations have finished.
Errors
No status is returned; destruction waits for in-flight internal work.
Threading
The pipeline state cache is thread-safe for concurrent requests; destruction waits for internal operations to finish. The bound RHI device must remain valid for the cache lifetime.

arda::backend::FArdaPipelineStateCache::GetOrCreateCompute
[[nodiscard]] rhi::FArdaRHIStatus GetOrCreateCompute( const FArdaComputePipelineStateInitializer& Initializer, rhi::FArdaRHIComputePipelineRef& OutPipeline, const rhi::IArdaRHIDevice* RequestingDevice = nullptr)

Resolves or creates a compute pipeline state.

Resolves or creates a compute pipeline state. Callers must inspect the returned status before relying on side effects. The operation does not mutate the observable state of the object through this interface.

Parameter
const FArdaComputePipelineStateInitializer& Initializer
Parameter
rhi::FArdaRHIComputePipelineRef& OutPipeline
Parameter
const rhi::IArdaRHIDevice* RequestingDevice = nullptr
Returns
RHI status for lookup or creation.
Ownership
Successful results are returned or bound through intrusive RHI references retained by the cache and caller-visible state. The optional requesting device is non-owning and used only for ownership validation.
Errors

function

arda::backend::InitializeBackendForPresentation
[[nodiscard]] EArdaInitializeResult InitializeBackendForPresentation( IArdaWindowSurface& WindowSurface, uint32_t Width, uint32_t Height, eastl::unique_ptr<IArdaSwapChain>& OutSwapChain)

Initializes the backend and a swap chain for a window surface.

Initializes an ArdaCreated backend and creates presentation resources through the supplied window-system adapter at the requested dimensions. The returned swap chain must be destroyed before ShutdownBackend. The current external-device wrapper is headless and host-presented: when mDeviceSource is ExternalProvider this function returns Failure, so the host must call InitializeBackend, import acquired frame images, and perform native presentation itself.

Parameter
IArdaWindowSurface& WindowSurface
Parameter
uint32_t Width
Parameter
uint32_t Height
Parameter
eastl::unique_ptr<IArdaSwapChain>& OutSwapChain
Returns
The backend initialization outcome.
Ownership
WindowSurface remains caller-owned. On success OutSwapChain receives unique ownership and must be destroyed before backend shutdown.
Errors
Returns Success, Unavailable, or Failure; platform surface creation can also write a diagnostic through the window-surface adapter. ExternalProvider mode returns Failure because external presentation is not implemented.
Threading
Process-wide backend configuration and lifetime operations must be externally serialized and must not run concurrently with device use.

arda::backend::IArdaSwapChain::AcquireFrame
[[nodiscard]] virtual bool AcquireFrame(rhi::FArdaRHIFramebufferRef& OutFramebuffer) = 0

Acquires the framebuffer for the next frame.

Acquires the framebuffer for the next frame. A false result makes OutFramebuffer unusable. Because the interface does not guarantee the failure-state value of the output across all backends, callers should clear OutFramebuffer before calling and inspect GetError after failure.

Parameter
rhi::FArdaRHIFramebufferRef& OutFramebuffer
Returns
True when a frame was acquired successfully.
Ownership
On success, OutFramebuffer receives an intrusive owning reference. On failure, treat the output as unusable regardless of its value; clear it before the call because failure output is not guaranteed consistently across backends.
Errors
False reports acquisition failure. Do not use OutFramebuffer after false; call GetError to inspect the observable swap-chain error.

arda::backend::IArdaSwapChain::PrepareSubmit
virtual void PrepareSubmit() = 0

Prepares presentation synchronization for submission of the acquired frame.

Prepares the currently acquired frame's presentation synchronization before queue submission; it does not replace resource-state transitions recorded by command lists. Call it in the required acquire, record, prepare-submit, submit, and present order. The operation is void and provides no immediate portable error result; observable failures surface later through Present, GetError, or the configured diagnostic callback.

Returns
No value.
Ownership
Does not transfer ownership. It operates on the swap chain's currently acquired frame and its presentation state.
Errors
No immediate portable error is returned. Preserve the required ordering, then observe failures through Present, GetError, or the configured diagnostic callback.

bool mbPipelineCachePersistence = false;

Reports whether the backend can persist native pipeline-cache data.

True means the concrete backend implements native cache loading and flushing when a non-empty pipeline-cache directory is configured. False does not disable the process-local FArdaPipelineStateCache object cache.

Errors
A false value requires callers to treat disk persistence as unavailable, not as a device initialization failure.

method

arda::rhi::FArdaRHICapabilities::IsQueueSupported
[[nodiscard]] bool IsQueueSupported(EArdaRHIQueueType Queue) const noexcept { switch (Queue) { case EArdaRHIQueueType::Graphics: return mbGraphicsQueue; case EArdaRHIQueueType::Compute: return mbComputeQueue; case EArdaRHIQueueType::Copy: return mbCopyQueue; } return false; }

Tests whether the queue supported.

Tests whether the queue supported. The operation is declared noexcept and must not propagate exceptions. The operation does not mutate the observable state of the object through this interface.

Parameter
EArdaRHIQueueType Queue
Returns

arda::rhi::IArdaRHICommandList::DecodeSamplerFeedbackTexture
virtual FArdaRHIStatus DecodeSamplerFeedbackTexture(IArdaRHITexture& Destination, IArdaRHISamplerFeedbackTexture& Texture, EArdaRHIFormat Format) = 0

Performs the decode sampler feedback texture operation.

Decodes all feedback subresources into an R8UInt Texture2D. The destination array size matches the paired texture; minimum-mip feedback needs one mip, and mip-region-used feedback needs the paired mip count. Width and height must each be at least ceil(paired extent / mip-region extent), with padding sufficient to allocate the required mip chain. The command transitions feedback to ResolveSource and destination to ResolveDest. Clear values decode to 0xFF for minimum-mip and zero for mip-region-used; a used region decodes to 0xFF.

Parameter
IArdaRHITexture& Destination
Parameter
IArdaRHISamplerFeedbackTexture& Texture
Parameter
EArdaRHIFormat Format
Returns
A status describing whether the operation succeeded.
Ownership
The command list retains the destination and feedback map, including the paired texture, through submission.
Errors

virtual FArdaRHIStatus ResizeDescriptorTable(const FArdaRHIDescriptorTableRef& Table, uint32_t NewSize, bool bKeepContents = true) = 0

Publishes a resized table version without changing previously recorded versions.

Table
Bindless descriptor table created by this device.
NewSize
Nonzero logical capacity no larger than the layout's maximum.
bKeepContents
Preserve in-range entries when true; otherwise clear the new version.
Returns
Success after replacement, InvalidArgument for size/descriptor errors, WrongDevice for invalid ownership, or a native allocation failure. Failure preserves the previous version.
Ownership
The new version retains its resources; recorded versions independently retain their previous dependencies through submission completion, including removed entries.
Errors
A null, foreign-device or incompatible table is rejected with WrongDevice.
Threading
Table updates and recording snapshots are serialized by the table mutex.

arda::rhi::IArdaRHIDevice::WriteDescriptorTable
virtual FArdaRHIStatus WriteDescriptorTable(const FArdaRHIDescriptorTableRef& Table, const FArdaRHIBindingItem& Item) = 0

Replaces one descriptor by publishing a retained table version.

Table
Bindless descriptor table created by this device.
Item
Same-device native resource and a declared slot/type/array element in range.
Returns
Success after replacement, WrongDevice for invalid ownership, InvalidArgument for an undeclared slot/type or invalid range, or a native allocation failure. Failure does not publish a partially changed table.
Ownership
A successful write retains Item.mResource immediately. Recorded versions keep their dependencies when subsequent writes replace entries; submission retains them until its own queue completes. No unsafe-lifetime opt-in is required.
Errors
WrongDevice rejects null/foreign resources and incompatible tables; InvalidArgument rejects undeclared slots or out-of-range array elements.
Threading
Table writes and command-list snapshots are serialized by the table mutex; resource data still needs ordinary GPU barriers and queue ordering.
Source

constructor

arda::rhi::TArdaRHIRef::TArdaRHIRef
constexpr TArdaRHIRef() noexcept = default

Constructs an empty or retained RHI object reference.

Constructs an empty or retained RHI object reference. The operation is declared noexcept and must not propagate exceptions. The operation does not mutate the observable state of the object through this interface.

Ownership
Constructs an empty reference and acquires no ownership.
Errors
No status is returned. Dereferencing an empty reference or violating transferred reference-count obligations is caller error.
Threading
TArdaRHIRef contains no synchronization. Concurrent access to the same reference object requires external synchronization; resource-level reference-count thread safety is implementation-defined.
Source

arda::rhi::FArdaRHIBindlessLayoutDesc::mbDescriptorBuffer
bool mbDescriptorBuffer = false

Uses native descriptor-buffer storage instead of descriptor sets.

Selects VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer storage. Query mDescriptors.mbDescriptorBuffer first. Every pipeline layout must select this mode, register spaces must be distinct, and native sampler/resource binding limits apply. Mutually exclusive with mbDirectHeapIndexing; unsupported providers reject the request.

Stores bindings in this public backend and RHI value.

Optional local binding set or descriptor table. Its layout must match the export's local layout and resources must belong to the same device. Vulkan local descriptors require VK_EXT_descriptor_heap and direct-heap layouts; classic global sets cannot be mixed with local heap descriptors. The captured native table version retains its resources.

arda::rhi::FArdaRHIShaderTableRecordDesc::mLocalArguments
eastl::vector<uint8_t> mLocalArguments

Stores local arguments in this public backend and RHI value.

Application local argument bytes validated against mMaxLocalArgumentBytes. With Vulkan local descriptor bindings, Arda prefixes these bytes with a 32-bit table base index; without local descriptor bindings there is no prefix. Explicit shader-record declarations combining bindings and arguments must account for the prefix. D3D12 places local descriptor handles before application arguments. Native shader identifiers are separate from these application bytes.

arda::rhi::IArdaRHIResource::AddRef
virtual void AddRef() noexcept = 0

Performs the add operation.

Increments the implementation-defined intrusive reference count that controls this resource lifetime.

Returns
No value.
Ownership
Adds one owning intrusive reference. Every successful AddRef obligation must eventually be balanced by Release.
Errors
No status is returned; the object must already be alive when called.
Threading
The interface does not state that reference counting is atomic; callers must follow the concrete implementation synchronization contract and must not race final Release with use.
Source

arda::rhi::IArdaRHIResource::GetCudaResourceInfo
[[nodiscard]] virtual FArdaCudaResourceInfo GetCudaResourceInfo() const noexcept

Reads CUDA representation facts qualified for this particular native allocation.

Returns
An owned value containing representation kind, sharing admission and available domains. Opaque AS/pipeline objects and ordinary nonshared allocations do not become CUDA-addressable merely because the device supports CUDA. The default is None/Graphics.
Ownership
Does not import, map, transfer ownership, or return a CUDA pointer.
Errors
Unsupported representations return the default value without failing or throwing.
Threading
Read-only allocation metadata; keep the resource alive during the call.

arda::rhi::IArdaRHIResource::Release
virtual void Release() noexcept = 0

Performs the release operation.

Drops one owning intrusive reference and may destroy the resource when the final reference is released.

Returns
No value.
Ownership
Releases one ownership claim. The pointer and all non-owning views must be treated as invalid if this was the final reference.
Errors
No status is returned; over-release, use after final release, and unbalanced ownership are caller errors.
Threading
The interface does not state that reference counting is atomic; callers must prevent races between final Release and all resource access.

arda::rhi::FArdaRHINativeBufferImportDesc::mLifetimeToken
eastl::shared_ptr<void> mLifetimeToken;

Optional shared token retained by the imported wrapper.

Optional shared token retained by the imported wrapper. The token, rather than Arda, owns any native lifetime it represents. Reusing the same native handle with a different token is a descriptor conflict for the imported resource cache.

Ownership
The shared token is copied and retained by the imported wrapper.
Errors
A different token for an already imported native handle is a descriptor conflict.
Threading
The host must synchronize raw native-handle use and destruction; Vulkan also requires external host synchronization.

Adds an overlay directory.

Registers an overlay directory beneath a virtual root. Exact repeats are idempotent; shared roots are allowed only when every discovered full virtual filename remains globally unique, including against nested exclusive mappings.

Parameter
const std::filesystem::path& RealDirectory
Parameter
const eastl::string& VirtualRoot = "/"
Returns
Registration status.
Ownership
Returned paths and strings are value snapshots; output path references remain caller-owned.
Errors
EArdaShaderDirectoryError distinguishes frozen or in-use state, invalid paths or directories, escaping files, unsupported extensions, duplicate or ambiguous mappings, scan failures, and missing virtual sources.
Threading
The process-wide shader directory registry must not be mutated concurrently. Mutations are rejected during backend initialization, while the backend is live, while shader registration uses the registry, or when frozen as specified by the operation.

arda::backend::FArdaGlobalShaderMap::Initialize
[[nodiscard]] bool Initialize( const FArdaDeviceContext& DeviceContext, const std::filesystem::path& ShaderDirectory)

Initializes the global shader map using an explicit artifact-directory override.

Commits shader registrations and uses ShaderDirectory instead of the configured persistent backend shader cache. Behavior then follows the configured EArdaShaderCompilationMode: OnDemand preallocates pointer-stable slots but leaves them unloaded until lookup or enumeration; Startup and LoadOnly eagerly materialize every selected slot by loading backend-specific bytecode and creating its RHI shader and parameter binding layouts. Repeating the same device context, backend, and directory is idempotent and pointer-stable; changing any of them after success requires Reset first.

Parameter
const FArdaDeviceContext& DeviceContext
Parameter
const std::filesystem::path& ShaderDirectory
Returns
True when registration and policy-specific initialization succeed.
Ownership
The map retains the RHI device, created shader references, binding layouts, directory, and instance storage until Reset or destruction. Returned instance pointers and references are non-owning views into that storage.
Errors
Returns false and records diagnostics for registration failure, invalid device, missing, empty, or unreadable bytecode, shader or layout creation failure, or a required Reset.
Threading
No concurrent mutation contract is declared; serialize Initialize and Reset with Find, Enumerate, diagnostics access, and device shutdown.
Source
Source/ArdaBackend/Public/ShaderStructs/ArdaGlobalShaderMap.h
arda::backend::FArdaGlobalShaderMap::Initialize
[[nodiscard]] bool Initialize(const FArdaDeviceContext& DeviceContext)

Initializes the global shader map using the configured persistent backend shader cache.

Commits shader registrations and uses FArdaBackendConfiguration::mShaderCacheDirectory. Behavior follows the configured EArdaShaderCompilationMode: OnDemand preallocates pointer-stable slots but leaves them unloaded until lookup or enumeration; Startup and LoadOnly eagerly materialize every selected slot by loading backend-specific bytecode and creating its RHI shader and parameter binding layouts. Repeating the same device context, backend, and configured directory is idempotent and pointer-stable; changing any of them after success requires Reset first.

Parameter
const FArdaDeviceContext& DeviceContext
Returns
True when registration and policy-specific initialization succeed.
Ownership
The map retains the RHI device, created shader references, binding layouts, directory, and stable instance-slot storage until Reset or destruction. Returned instance pointers and references are non-owning views into that storage.
Errors
Returns false and records diagnostics for registration failure, invalid device, missing, empty, or unreadable bytecode, shader or layout creation failure, or a required Reset.
Threading
No concurrent mutation contract is declared; serialize Initialize and Reset with Find, Enumerate, diagnostics access, and device shutdown.
Source

Validates and publishes all pending shader type registrations.

Validates every pending registration against unique names and identities, parameter metadata, and the frozen shader-source manifest, then publishes committed shader types in deterministic order.

arda::backend::FArdaShaderTypeRegistration::ResetForTests
static void ResetForTests()

Test-only reset that makes static shader registration nodes pending again.

Test-only API. Applications must not call this function: it clears committed registry state and requeues static registration nodes, invalidating normal shader-registration lifecycle assumptions.

Returns
No value.
Ownership
Does not destroy static registration nodes; it changes their process-wide registry state.
Errors
No status is returned. Calling it during application use can invalidate lookups and global shader initialization assumptions.
Threading
Tests must call this only with exclusive access, no active backend or global shader map, and no concurrent registry readers.
